records.c: Relocates the picture unpacker to the stack page and low RAM, changes the CPU port and jumps to the unpacker at $0100. The picture paths enter it at $0813.
Banks out I/O and ROMs. Relocates two 166-byte source windows into low memory, then jumps to the unpacker at $0100.
The first copy reads $082A plus Y. The loop stops before Y equals zero, so its first actual source byte is $082B.
Satellite over earth package offsets $0019–$0418. This span starts with bytes relocated into low RAM by the bootstrap and continues into the packed picture stream.

The bootstrap at $081F copies $08D1–$0976 to $0334–$03D9 for the unpacker. These bytes are in the packed satellite over Earth package. The rest of this span supplies the picture decoder until the next boundary at $0C00.
On entry this holds the packed first picture. After the depacker runs, $0C00 is the expanded VIC screen-attribute source.
Packed satellite over Earth data at package offsets $0419–$0818. The picture unpacker reads these bytes while populating the colour, screen-attribute and bitmap planes.
On entry these bytes still belong to the packed first picture. Expanded bitmap output occupies $1000 after the depacker runs.
Packed satellite over Earth data at package offsets $0819–$0C18. The picture unpacker reads these bytes while populating the colour, screen-attribute and bitmap planes.
Packed satellite over Earth data at package offsets $0C19–$0D76. The picture unpacker reads these bytes while populating the colour, screen-attribute and bitmap planes.
The last 192 bytes in the page-aligned bitmap staging region. The 8,000-byte rendered plane ends at $2F3F. The full-page display copies may transfer part of this zero tail beyond the visible cells.
Sets up the display and music, resets SP and makes its first bitmap display call.
Low operand of the colour-source read. Increments by forty when the fill moves to the following row.
Low operand for the first scene’s highlight writes in colour RAM. The routine shades the area and uses fire to skip the intervening delay.
Switches to the low-bank picture, masks and restores the bottom screen rows, plays the first overlay, then changes banks for the next overlays.
Copies the next picture into the low VIC bank, clears the screen and colour strip and runs the third sprite sequence.
Switches to the high VIC bank, updates screen colours with the banking controlled around the stores, runs the fourth sprite sequence and requests the fade.
Pushes the synthetic return $2FFF, selects file $0E with two blocks and jumps to $0433. The loader returns to $3000 in the new image.
Three zero bytes after the jump into the loader and before the next display helper.
Prepares the VIC and copies the expanded attributes, bitmap and colours to $6000, $4000 and $D800. Selects VIC bank $4000 and D018=$80.
Selects a packed picture, copies its screen attributes to RAM under $DC00 and the bitmap to $E000, fills colour RAM at $D800 and selects VIC bank $C000.
Selects the two-byte address from the scene table. The next-picture path increments the index.
Little-endian source addresses for the 5 packed picture programs. The selector indexes with twice the scene number and copies the selected source beginning at $0812.
This base reads the high byte of the picture address at twice the selected scene index. The corresponding low byte is read one address earlier.
Stored $FFFF immediately after the 5 valid picture addresses.
Uses the scene number to select a two-byte source pointer and copies 23 pages into the staging area beginning at $0812.
Low byte of the packed-picture copy’s source operand, set from the selected scene pointer.
High byte of the packed-picture source. The copy increments this after each 256-byte page.
Page byte of the destination operand. Resets to $08 for each picture and advances after each copied page.
Calls the picture depacker at $0813 and restores $35 in the CPU port so the display routines can access I/O.
Copies X plus one full pages to the selected display plane. Increments the source and destination pages as each page completes.
High source operand for the display copy. The caller selects $08, $0C or $10 according to the plane.
High destination operand for the page copier, selected by expected display plane and VIC bank.
Initializes the raster-count loop at $3273. A fresh active-low fire press can exit early.
Waits for each raster pass and tests CIA fire. A new press can end the current delay and the latch prevents another skip until release.
Tracks whether this wait routine has already consumed the held fire press.
Waits for raster low byte zero and then for it to become nonzero.
Clears the I/O address range $D400–$D7FF, then zeros $02–$FF. Preserves the processor port bytes $00 and $01.
High-byte operand that the I/O clear loop increments up to $D8.
Selects frame table, length, sprite bias and palette by sequence. Displays the first frame, waits the initial delay, advances through the frame limit and waits the final delay.
Copies the frame delay into $0E and counts transitions out of raster line low byte $F1 until the delay expires.
Computes 24 times the 16-bit frame index as eight times plus sixteen times, then adds the sequence table address.
Immediate operand holding the incoming X during frame-record address calculation.
Each 24-byte record names eight Y values, eight X values and eight shape indices. Skips slots with Y=$FF. A shape's last byte controls both expansion flags, multicolour and palette index.
Operand of the addition that translates the per-slot shape index into a VIC pointer, patched for the sequence.
High byte of the indexed sprite-pointer store. The sequence chooses the low or high VIC bank’s screen pointer page.
Converts the 8-bit VIC sprite pointer in A into a 16-bit byte offset in $0B/$0C using two right shifts and rotations.
High operand patched for reading a sprite shape’s expansion and palette flags in the selected VIC bank.
Eight powers of two used to update the VIC enable, expansion and multicolour flags for each sprite slot.
Low byte of the sprite frame-table address. Stored sequence values are $96, $DE, $7E, $AD.
High byte of the sprite frame-table address. Stored sequence values are $BE, $C4, $CA, $9F.
Number of raster waits per animation step, copied to $0D. Stored sequence values are $02, $06, $04, $06.
Highest frame index the playback loop selects. Stored sequence values are $42, $3B, $2E, $2E.
Patched high byte of the VIC screen’s sprite-pointer store. Stored sequence values are $63, $DF, $63, $DF.
Value added to each raw shape index before programming the display pointer. Stored sequence values are $B0, $50, $90, $50.
Number of frame delays used to hold the first frame before advancing. Stored sequence values are $01, $01, $01, $01.
Number of frame delays used to hold the final frame before returning. Stored sequence values are $01, $01, $01, $01.
Page bias for reading a sprite’s flag byte from the selected VIC bank. Stored sequence values are $40, $C0, $40, $C0.
Value programmed into $D025 when this sequence begins. Stored sequence values are $00, $01, $0F, $01.
Value programmed into $D026 when this sequence begins. Stored sequence values are $00, $0B, $00, $00.
Selects RAM vectors and I/O access, masks both CIA interrupt sources, clears SID volume and disables VIC interrupts.
Installs IRQ $BE59 and NMI $BE91, enables VIC raster triggers and selects line 200.
Zero bytes separating the end of the IRQ vector setup from the video rate wrapper at $3500.
Tests $02A6 and can redirect the raster’s music call to the scene divider. Then quiets the machine for the scene.
The wrapper at $3500 installs this target when $02A6 is zero. Decrements the countdown operand at $3514 and calls $B003. When it expires, reloads six and returns.
Immediate byte used as the divider countdown. It is decremented until the update is skipped and the counter is reloaded.
The satellite interrupt wrapper ends at $3522. The loaded zero gap runs up to the next packed scene at $4000. The depacker explicitly writes zero at $3523–$3922.
